thesis: Evolutionary levels, motives and institutional distributions resist a universal law that kindness loses.
role: The animal that cannot win alone

ideas.statement: Promotion, reproduction and cultural transmission differ; education-associated genetic findings do not measure goodness or dictate reproductive duties.
Cooperation mechanisms depend on information, repeated interaction and exit; exploitation can consume trust others create, and cooperation can harm outsiders.
Origins and beneficial consequences do not exhaust motives; love and exploitation can both be real, and vulnerability can arise from value.
Group survival may distribute costs unevenly; prestige differs from dominance, honors may replace reform, and saints can help construct indispensability.
